title: Scan store says whether any folder at or below a given folder is still unlisted
how_to_read: Each attempt is one line and a `details` filename in this same directory. Open a detail file ONLY when this index points you at one -- the summaries are here so you do not have to. `caused_by` is what sent the stage back; `changed` is what the attempt then touched, counted by kind. Several attempts in a row that were caused by the same stage and changed no `src` is a loop, not progress.

open.issue: 1. For every folder in stores stopped at many points on real temp trees, the store's answer matches a full walk of everything below that folder: missing
2. The answer relies on the shipped traversal (one writer, depth-first, each folder's children one block); a test fails if that traversal is changed to a queue or made parallel: missing
3. Answering for every row of an open 100k-child folder fits inside the 0.5 s open budget (timing test on a 5M-entry synthetic store stopped late, with a 100k-child folder): missing
4. A scan that runs to the end reports nothing unlisted below any folder (core test on completed scans of real temp trees): missing
5. The answer adds no per-entry storage; a 5M-entry store stopped late stays within the 800 MiB store bound (memory test at 5M entries in U-201's shape): missing

Derived (from 'the store can say, for any folder'): a public read on ScanStore in Core, exact on the same terms as NotListed (between appends on the writing thread, and after Scan has returned): missing

Derived (from the SC-367 merge note): SL-111's design records that the answer holds only while the traversal stays depth-first, and that a Kind-bit marker would need masking across the seven Kind reads: missing
The name NotListedAtOrBelow, against AnyNotListedAtOrBelow or SubtreeUnfinished. Uncontested; the reviewer may prefer another.
Placement in ScanStore.cs beside NotListed, rather than in ScanStore.Rollup.cs. The rationale is Rollup.cs's 'never walks below' header, but it is a layering call.
A new NotListedBelowTests.cs that reaches into NotListedTests' now-internal sweep helpers, against putting the new Theories inside NotListedTests (or a shared fixture class).
Self-inclusive 'at or below', against U-204's strict-descendant reading. This is a semantic choice with no consumer yet.
A Kind-byte architecture rule as a tripwire for a future Kind-bit marker. A reviewer may judge it premature, since U-201 shows masking makes the marker valid.
The architecture rule 'the store writes the Kind byte whole' in .taad/fitness.yaml: dropped by review m1's disposition and replaced by KindByteWriteCorpusTests and its corpus.

A 100,000-entry on-disk fixture for a Stop inside a real folder listing (C-014, material:false in the design): not worth 28-30 s against Q-222's 120 s cap. The multi-buffer 'big' folder takes the same branch, and the real-scan run below also covered Stops mid-listing.
The straddling-page Fact (m4, waived to SC-395), the forward-progress throw (m5, waived to SC-396), and the Scanner.cs comments (m6, waived to SC-397).
No App wiring: FolderTreeNode and the row text are untouched, so T-003 and the window cases and WindowMutants are not in play. Showing the answer on stopped-tree rows is filed for the next slice.

Show the subtree-unread answer on stopped-tree and stopped-list rows in the App (FolderTreeNode and row text), with the window cases, T-003 (red at HEAD) and Q-114's WindowMutants run for an App diff.

Before any pause/resume, read-ahead, block-wise flush or parallel-listing slice changes registration, it must keep depth-first preorder with one SetChildren per whole block (and add a sweep folder larger than one flush block), or replace NotListedAtOrBelow with a stored pending-subfolder count and a 5M memory test. SC-395 (page-straddling block), SC-396 (forward-progress throw) and SC-397 (comments at Scanner._pending and FolderDone) carry the waived findings.

deviation: Design says add a Kind-byte fitness rule. Review m1 (accepted-pending) overrode that: no .taad/fitness.yaml change, so no Q-027 rules-harness run. The marker class (O-015) is held by a test-backed closed-grammar corpus instead, because O-015 requires a corpus whose rows pass. The design doc lists the spellings the grammar cannot see.

deviation: Design says the criterion-1 sweep stops through Scans.RunCancellingAt. Per m2, the sweep-tree theory stops through NotListedTests.StopAt, so m\Layers is planted, and asserts a NotScanned Layers stop. Options and StopAt are made internal alongside the other fixtures.

deviation: Design says the criterion-5 test builds no oracle array. It builds none. The allocation counter is read after one warm-up call, and the bound is 64 KiB rather than exactly 0; the measured figure was 0 bytes.

deviation: Design says the read goes over 'the page arrays'. Per m4 (waived to SC-395), the backward scan looks up each entry's page on its own (_pages[c >> PageShift]) so a block straddling a page boundary reads the right page. The straddling-block Fact itself is not built, as waived.

deviation: The m5 loop-termination guard (throw if a chain step does not move forward) and the m6 comment-only notes at Scanner._pending and FolderDone were waived to SC-396 and SC-397 and are not built. Scanner.cs is untouched.

O-014 not done: Not handed to this stage; it is owed to validate-slice. The order is guarded by TheScannerRegistersFoldersDepthFirstInListingOrder, the sweeps and the replays, and recorded in the design doc and the NotListedAtOrBelow doc comment.

drift: The criterion-1 non-vacuity floor is written as `listedTrue >= stores - rootsNotListed` (NotListedBelowTests.cs:218, :301). The design says 'the number of listed folders reading true is at least the number of stops that left a root'. That is weaker than the literal wording, but the literal floor cannot be met: a store whose root is NotListed holds no listed folder. Not declared.

drift: The criterion-3 Fact asserts NotListedAtOrBelow on root, A, S and Pad (ScanStoreRollupTimingTests.cs:170-171) before its timed passes, so the 'first pass cold' that the design and matrix row describe is cold for data but not for the read's JIT. Not declared. Immaterial: the first pass was 58.3 ms against 250 ms.

drift: KindByteWriteCorpusTests' closed grammar also refuses read spellings it does not know (`is (byte)EntryKind.X`, a read into a local; corpus Q13 and Q14). Any later Store/** edit that adds such a read goes red until the grammar is edited. This is declared in the design doc (:107-108), recorded here so the next Store slice expects it.

not reviewed: .taad/slices/SL-111/design-slice-1.json, critique-1.json, critique-review-1.json, build-slice-1.json: stage records, not code. Not opened, following the instruction to judge the code independently of other stages' accounts. index.json was only skimmed for caused_by/changed, and shows no loop.
not reached: A whole-drive or multi-million-entry real scan with Stops. The 5M figures (criteria 3 and 5) are synthetic stores; the largest real store here was 100,011 entries.
not reached: A reader on another thread while the scanner appends. That is outside the read's contract and was not exercised.
not reached: A real parallel, read-ahead or pause/resume scanner. None exists, so criterion 2's 'made parallel' rests on replays.
not reached: A registration made block by block (a SetChildren per flush block) inside a folder larger than one block. The tests would not catch it (O-020, waived to SC-397).

not reached: A block straddling a page boundary where a wrong page would change the answer. It is not deterministically tested (SC-395). The 100k real folder's block does cross the boundary and read correctly, but only for a folder with no subfolders.
not reached: Windows 10, ReFS/FAT, SMB shares and cloud-placeholder folders. Everything ran on local NTFS, Windows 11 26200.
not reached: Any App consumer of the read. Nothing in src calls NotListedAtOrBelow yet, so no person has seen the answer on screen.
not reached: Criterion 3 timing in a Release build (only Debug was run here; spike 121 measured Release at 29 ms).

code-review missed: KindByteWriteCorpusTests Grammar.Check strips comments with two regexes that do not tokenise C#. A `//` or `/*` inside a string literal, a `/*` inside a `//` comment (a cited glob such as tests/*.cs with a later src/**/x), and a `//` comment ended by U+2028 or U+0085 each blank live code, so a Kind-byte marker write in that text gets 0 refusals. Round 1 only mutated the read and the Scanner. It never fed the one new parser the diff added. Check it should have run: feed the grammar the six lines above and require a refusal.

critique missed: The design's criterion-1 non-vacuity floor ('listed folders reading true >= stops that left a root') cannot be met, because a store whose root is NotListed holds no listed folder. The critique should have asked whether the floor is satisfiable in the stops that leave only a root. The builder silently rewrote it as `listedTrue >= stores - rootsNotListed` (NotListedBelowTests.cs:218, :301).

critique missed: The design says the criterion-3 test's first pass is cold, but its own asserted shape (root, A and S read true, Pad false) runs the read before the timed passes. The first pass is cold for data and warm for the read's JIT. The critique checked that each criterion had a case with a command, not that the cold claim survived the test's own setup.

still unknown: Why is window case T-003 red at HEAD (design and build-check both cite it, via lesson #505), and does a backlog item already cover it? SC-393 touches FolderTreeNode, so Q-128 requires T-003 at its validate and a red T-003 would block it.

still unknown: What does the read cost on a real large store? The largest real store in this slice was 100,011 entries, and the 5M figures (51.0 ms worst pass, Debug only) are synthetic. Spike 121 measured Release at 29 ms. Does a real C:\ tree (about 1M folders) with a 100k-child folder keep the whole open under the window's 0.5 s once SC-393 wires the App?

still unknown: Does the engine require a corpus to discharge a class_of obligation? The build read O-015 as 'requires a corpus whose rows pass', although m1's disposition asked only for prose in the design doc. If prose would have discharged it, the 57-test lexer was avoidable.

went wrong: Build attempt 1 halted on the provider's session limit with a built but unreviewed tree and no design record (docs/design/SL-111-not-listed-below.md). Attempt 2 had to audit and then trust it. It was sound, but the audit was a lap of its own.

went wrong: m1's disposition said to drop the fitness rule and list the escapes in the design doc. The build instead wrote a closed-grammar C# lexer, a 55-row JSON corpus and a census, because O-015 was closed as a class. That is 57 of the 65 new tests, none serving a numbered criterion. The lexer was the only parser in the diff and it was wrong (R2-R2-1).

went wrong: O-015 was closed as a whole family ('Kind-byte marker write spellings') and then a missing member of the family was found in the same slice. It was waived to SC-398 as 'does not weigh a lap'. The class was known to be incomplete at ship time.

went wrong: The first code-review round returned 'found nothing that needs fixing'. Only the second round found the one real defect, in the test-side grammar. Round 1 mutated the production read and the Scanner and never attacked the new parser.

went wrong: Lesson #485 named the gap that the order dependency is written only in a doc comment and a design doc. Critique m6 re-found it and the disposition accepted it, but the build waived it (SC-397). Scanner.cs:168 and FolderDone still carry no warning. The same gap was named three times and not built.

went wrong: Three of six critique findings (m4, m5, m6) were waived at build. m5 is a single comparison that would turn a malformed-block hang into a throw. m4 was built in the read (per-entry page lookup) but its straddling-page Fact was not. All six critique findings were minor and were dispositioned by a model, so they count as untriaged.

went wrong: Validate's Scanner mutation left a mutated Core DLL in bin\Debug after git checkout. The first real-folder run used it and showed 13 of 31 stopped stores wrong at the root. Validate noticed, disclosed it and re-ran clean (0 differences), but the run was wasted.

went wrong: The design's own text was inconsistent in two places the critique passed: an unsatisfiable non-vacuity floor, and a 'cold first pass' that its own pre-timing asserts warm. The builder changed the floor without declaring it, and code review had to flag both as drift.
